expected.summary: A staged rollout of checkout 2.0.0-rc1 reached three of six pods (one every two minutes from ten minutes before the anchor) and paused for canary observation; the deployment.rollout logs name the updated pods checkout-1 through checkout-3. The new build assumes every promo code has a percentOff field, so fixed-amount codes (FREESHIP, FLAT5, GIFT10) throw TypeError in applyPromotion and the request 500s before payment is called. Only the three updated pods fail, only for fixed-amount promo codes. Errors propagate to the BFFs and edge-gateway, which is where the alert fires. payment completed its own 3.7.0 rollout ten minutes earlier and is healthy on both versions. The new checkout build also emits a DeprecationWarning WARN flood with no relation to the failures.
contributingFactors: fixed-amount promo codes hit the broken applyPromotion path

criteria.description: Does the brief identify the checkout 2.0.0-rc1 staged rollout, whose applyPromotion throws a TypeError (undefined percentOff) on fixed-amount promo codes on the updated pods, as the origin, with edge-gateway as the place the alert fired rather than the cause? 5 = the complete chain including the paused rollout at 3/6 and the promo-code trigger. 'There was a deploy' without the promo trigger caps at 2.

Is the conclusion grounded in the pod split (failures confined to checkout-1..3, the pods the deployment.rollout logs name) and the trace-correlated TypeError stack? Cap at 3 unless the rollout log join is explicit and the onset is dated at the first pod flip.

Does the brief avoid blaming payment's completed 3.7.0 rollout (healthy on both versions, and failed checkouts never reach payment), the DeprecationWarning WARN flood (no trace correlation to the 500s), or edge-gateway itself? Cap at 3 unless payment and the WARN flood are both dismissed with evidence.
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
